reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not directly support the key premises. E1 only notes that dual-phase HEAs have distinctive phase boundaries and that deformation mechanisms are not well understood, without showing that annealing modifies boundaries or reduces pile-ups. E2 discusses thermo-mechanical processing of a different EHEA composition (AlCoCrFeNi2.1) and mentions property improvements via complex processing, but provides no evidence that a simple annealing step modifies semi-coherent boundaries to relieve dislocation pile-ups in the claimed alloy.
premises: Semi-coherent phase boundaries in as-cast AlCoCrFeNi cause dislocation pile-ups and stress concentration.
Thermal annealing can modify these semi-coherent boundaries to reduce dislocation pile-ups.
Annealing can relieve internal stress and smooth dislocation accumulation without coarsening the lamellar structure.
Modified boundaries will delay crack initiation and improve ductility while preserving strength.
